subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should the shared reply pipeline suppress the whole message for generic prefix text followed by `NO_REPLY`, or keep delivering substantive-looking prefixes except for narrower reasoning/cron/token-only cases?
rationale: Current source and tests deliberately preserve some substantive trailing-token replies, while this issue asks to turn that same shape into full suppression for security and noise reduction; automation cannot safely choose that policy boundary.

options.title: Define A Narrow Shared Silence Rule
options.body: Suppress whole messages only for an explicit final-line or silent-intent boundary that maintainers document, and add tests for both suppression and preserved substantive replies.

options.title: Adopt Broad Contains Suppression
options.body: Treat any `NO_REPLY` occurrence as a whole-message suppressor, accepting the message-loss risk for text that previously delivered after token stripping.

options.title: Preserve Current Split Behavior
options.body: Keep the current reasoning-prefixed, punctuation token-only, and cron-specific fixes, then close or re-scope this issue as not planned for generic mixed content.

recommendation.title: Define A Narrow Shared Silence Rule
recommendation.body: Suppress whole messages only for an explicit final-line or silent-intent boundary that maintainers document, and add tests for both suppression and preserved substantive replies.

likelyOwner.reason: The previous review and related timeline already route the remaining shared reply-suppression policy choice to this person after recent partial fixes.
